newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin conscious, still on respirator - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin conscious, still on respirator - spokesman.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin has recovered consciousness after heart surgery and opened his eyes, but will remain on a respirator overnight, Kremlin press spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said on Tuesday.

Speaking live on NTV television, he said the news came from Professor Yevgeny Chazov, head of the Cardiology Research Centre where Yeltsin underwent a seven-hour bypass operation. He gave no further details of the president's condition.
Yastrzhembsky said he spoke to Chazov by telephone at 6.45 p.m. (1545 GMT).
Doctors treating Yeltsin would issue a bulletin on Wednesday after meeting at 9 a.m. (0600 GMT), he added.
He said Yeltsin and his doctors would decide at a later stage whether to accept invitations from the governments of Germany and Slovakia to travel abroad for convalescence.
Meanwhile Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, standing in for Yeltsin, spoke by telephone on Tuesday to foreign leaders who called to enquire about Yeltsin's condition, his press service said.
Chernomyrdin spoke to U.S. President Bill Clinton, German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, French President Jacques Chirac, Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma and Kazakhstan President Nursultan Nazarbayev.
